ConnectionStrings.// Rekfar: Empty on purpose — the API refuses to start without it. Locally: dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:Rekfar" "Server=localhost,1433;Database=Rekfar;..." --project src/Rekfar.Api. In Azure the logical server is Entra-only, so there is no password to store — the container app authenticates as its managed identity, named explicitly rather than left to DefaultAzureCredential's probing chain: Server=tcp:rekfar.database.windows.net,1433;Database=Rekfar;Authentication=Active Directory Managed Identity;User Id=<identity-client-id>;Encrypt=True;. Set there by infra/main.bicep, not by hand — see docs/operations.md.

Database.// CommandTimeoutSeconds: Above the 30s ADO.NET default. The free-offer database is serverless and auto-pauses, so the first query after an idle period waits on a resume that can take tens of seconds.

Cors.// AllowedOrigins: Deliberately empty: the API refuses to start without an explicit origin, and every environment names its own. Note that configuration merges arrays by index, so a non-empty default here would leak entries into environments that override only the first.

Hosting.// TrustForwardedHeaders: True only where an ingress overwrites X-Forwarded-For. Trusting it anywhere else lets a caller forge the address the rate limiter partitions on.

RateLimiting.//: Per caller, per window, on /v1 only. A map client refetches on every pan and zoom, so this has to clear normal browsing comfortably — it is here to stop abuse, not to shape traffic.

Security.// AntiForgeryHeader: Required on every state-changing request under /v1. The session cookie is SameSite=None, so a cross-site form post would otherwise carry it; a header a page cannot set without a CORS preflight is what separates the client from an attacker. Empty disables the requirement, which is only sensible where the client is same-site with the API.

Auth.//: The session clock and the caps on a sign-in code. These are decisions (ADR-0017, user-accounts-mvp-plan §7), not defaults that happened — they are configurable so a test can collapse a window, not because a deployment is expected to disagree.
Auth.// SessionDays: Sliding, renewed on use, with no absolute cap in Phase 1. Passwordless makes an expired session cost an email round-trip rather than a remembered password.
Auth.// SecurityStampValidationSeconds: How often a live session is re-checked against the user's security stamp. This interval IS the window in which a session revoked by 'sign out everywhere' still works.
Auth.// CookieSameSite: None where the client is not same-site with the API, which is the deployed shape: the SPA is on Netlify and the API on Azure Container Apps. Lax where they share a registrable domain.
Auth.// MaxVerificationAttempts: Guesses one address gets before verification stops answering for it — which is how a code is invalidated (ADR-0017).
Auth.// MaxCodeRequestsPerAddress: Codes one inbox may be sent per window. Per address, so a flood aimed at one person is stopped even when it comes from many clients (NFR-SEC-4).
Auth.// UsedCodeMemoryMinutes: How long a spent code is remembered, so it cannot be used twice. Must outlast the window in which Identity would still accept it.
Auth.// CodeRequestRateLimit: The per-caller half of NFR-SEC-4, far below the general /v1 limit: nobody signs in ten times an hour.

Email.//: Azure Communication Services Email (ADR-0018). Empty here on purpose: infra/main.bicep sets Endpoint and SenderAddress from the resource it creates, and the API refuses to start in Production without them. Locally they stay empty and the code is written to the log instead of being sent.
Email.// ManagedIdentityClientId: Named rather than discovered, for the reason the connection string gives. Empty falls back to DefaultAzureCredential, which is what a developer signed in with `az login` wants.
